thread:
Maya: Heads-up: dashboard widget caching is causing RBAC surprises in staging — users see counts they shouldn't after role changes.
Jon: ugh, yep seen that. Is this the per-widget edge cache we added last sprint?
Maya: yup. Edge CDN TTL = 10m. Problem: when we change a user's roles or a policy, cached responses don't reflect the new permissions.
Priya: a few ways to handle: invalidate every time policy/user role changes (hard), make cache key include auth context (role idset/hash) (medium), or move to server-side filtered caches per-role (expensive).
Alex: also worth noting: most dashboard widgets are aggregation-heavy (count by model/route). Full per-user keys blow up cache cardinality. We measured ~x100 increase in keys in staging.
Jon: tradeoffs: 1) strong correctness: per-principal keys + short TTL -> correct but huge mem usage and cache churn. 2) correctness w/ lower cardinality: include role-set hash + policy-version in key -> smaller but still grows with many role combos. 3) eventual consistency: keep current edge cache but invalidate on role change events -> risk small window of leak.
Maya: product asks for correctness (no leaks). also ops wants not to double infra spend.
Priya: proposal: cache key = widget_id + query_sig + role_hash + policy_version. role_hash = hash(sorted(role_ids)) so identical role combinations dedupe. policy_version increments on any RBAC policy change for org. TTL = 5m. plus immediate async invalidation job that bumps policy_version for affected orgs on role changes.
Jon: that solves correctness for role changes (policy_version bump) and keeps key cardinality tied to unique role combinations vs users. neat. Edge-case: user-specific attributes (row-level perms tied to user id) still require per-user keys. do we have many of those?
Alex: only a few customers use row-level per-user filters. For those, we can opt-out of edge/CDN caching and keep server-side memcache with per-principal keys and shorter TTL.
Maya: what about cache poisoning / auth replay — if role_hash isn't bound to a tenant, could different orgs collide?
Priya: include org_id in the key prefix. also include a signed cache-salt per org to avoid accidental collisions across deployments.
Jon: sample key snippet: 
```
cache_key = f"{org_id}:{widget_id}:{query_sig}:{policy_version}:{role_hash}"
```
Alex: performance numbers: for 1M base keys, adding role_hash + policy_version pushes to ~1.3M in staging (acceptable). Per-user keys would be 40M -> unaffordable.
Maya: invalidation flow?
Priya: on role/policy update we emit event to infra-invalidation topic. Invalidation service computes affected orgs/widgets and increments policy_version for the org (atomic). Edge cache respects policy_version embedded in keys so new requests will get fresh keys. We also push a soft purge (CDN key purge) for hot widgets.
Jon: do we need strong sync purge for critical changes (e.g., revoke access immediately)?
Maya: yes, for access revocation we need near-immediate effect. Proposal: critical changes trigger immediate CDN purge + policy_version bump + flag to mark user session for reauth. Non-critical changes can rely on moral eventual consistency via TTL + policy_version bump.
Alex: ops: purge rate limits on CDN are a concern. we'll only purge top-N active widgets per org to avoid abuse. rest fall back to policy_version TTL.
Priya: audit: log policy_version changes with who triggered and diff of policies so we can forensics. Also telemetry to count cache hits/misses by role_hash to detect explosion.
Maya: owners? Priya to design key format + invalidation service contract, Alex to run perf tests and ops cost estimate, Jon to add integration hooks in query layer and console API. I'll coordinate product acceptance criteria.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: infra/invalidation-service v0.1 -> canary at 2026-03-24 15:00 UTC.
Jon: one last note — if customers want stricter isolation we should recommend dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) where caches are per-tenant and easier to control. include in docs.
Maya: OK let's roll with role_hash + policy_version + 5m TTL + async invalidation + targeted CDN purge for critical -> follow-ups on PRs and runbook.
Priya: will sketch RFC and post here tomorrow.
Alex: +1
Maya: :thumbsup:
